newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - H.K. Newspaper headlines - Nov 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - H.K. Newspaper headlines - Nov 12.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- HONG KONG DAILY NEWS -- Beijing has decided to maintain the Xinhua News Agency as its senior representative body in Hong Kong for a period after the handover, but a ministerial level appointee, senior to the present director Zhou Nan, will head the agency.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- A speech by Chinese President Jiang Zemin at a grand conference held to commemorate the 130th anniversary of the birth of Sun Yat-sen will be broadcast live
-- China's Vice Foreign Minster Tang Jiaxuan said that the Foreign Ministry will set up a Hong Kong operation after the handover.
-- APPLE DAILY -- The Government has asked China Light and Power to postpone the construction of Black Point station to reduce excessive power capacity.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin and Premier Li Peng are locked in an internal struggle for dominance over foreign policy in the lead-up to a major reshuffle of party and government leadership in the next two years.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Hong Kong tycoon Li Ka-shing said he planned to step back gradually in 1998 and leave the running of his businesses to his sons.

-- MING PAO DAILY -- Despite the implementation of stricter regulations in August, bad debts incurred by Chinese banks had increased and now total close to 2,000 billion yuan, representing about 25 per cent of total loans.
-- Communist Party newspapers are trying to stave off financial difficulties by setting up evening editions carrying lifestyle stories to attract readers.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Chief Executive contender Yang Ti Liang said the Democratic Party was not as anti-China as some people had suggested.
-- One of the first mainland companies to list on Wall Street, the Huaneng Power International, is seeking a secondary listing in Hong Kong.
-- Representatives of the territory's pension fund industry will urge the Government not to impose investment restrictions on the planned Mandatory Provident Fund.
-- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843-6441
"We should hold below 110-10, otherwise we'll see it push all the way to 111-00, the channel target," Miller said.
Support this session is around 108-25, a trendline from September which contained all of last week's trading, she said.
"We actually still favour it giving way through 108-25 once we see this short up-break and are looking for it down towards 108-05, then 107-29 -- channel support," she said.

Miranda Churchill, technical analyst at Light Blue Trading Bahamas in London said a convincing close above the top of the channel around 109-19 would give the contract a chance to target the high at 111-17.
"We could a see test of that if we get a close above the channel but I'm not looking for a break of that at the moment," she said. "I don't think we've got enough upside in the other markets.
Churchill said more immediately, a break above the channel would allow a run at the double top in October at 110-11 and 110-10.
March short sterling futures were quoted at 93.37, up 0.02 from Monday's settlement.
